title: Ki Tavo: a heart to know (Deuteronomy 29:3)
hookLine: only after forty years are they given "a heart to know"

lines: ONLY NOW, A HEART FOR IT.
cards: A mother tells her fifteen-year-old something, and gets an eye-roll. Fifteen years later the daughter is standing in her own kitchen, and the sentence comes back, and this time it lands. It wasn't wrong back then.
She just didn't have the heart for it yet. Near the end of Ki Tavo, Moses says something like this to a whole people. Forty years in, he tells them they're only now ready to understand.

teach.b: Moses reminds them of everything they saw: the plagues in Egypt, the signs, the great wonders.

teach.h: LEV LADA'AT: A HEART TO KNOW.
teach.b: And then: "But the LORD hath not given you a heart to know, and eyes to see, and ears to hear, unto this day." Forty years of wonders, and only now, at the edge of the river, a heart to know. In Hebrew, lev lada'at.
In the Hebrew Bible the heart isn't mainly the seat of feelings. It's where a person thinks, understands and decides. A heart to know is a mind that can finally take it in.
Rashi draws a lesson from the timing.

teach.h: FORTY YEARS TO GRASP A TEACHER.
teach.b: He brings a teaching found in the Talmud: a student does not fully grasp the mind of a teacher until forty years have passed. The people have had Moses for forty years.
Now, in his last days, they're ready to understand him.
The Mishnah, in Pirkei Avot, lists the ages of a life, and one line says: at forty, understanding. Some things can't be hurried by effort.

You can memorize a text in a week; understanding it waits for the years that make it make sense. That isn't a failure of the student. It's how understanding works: seeing comes first, and knowing can take years.

how: Jewish learning is traditionally lifelong: the same texts are studied again and again over decades, often with the same teacher or study partner, on the expectation that understanding deepens with age.

s: in the Hebrew Bible, the heart is only about feelings
it's where a person thinks, understands and decides.
Moses says they weren't given a heart to know until that day
Rashi says a student grasps a teacher's mind after forty days

games.q: you've studied a hard text for months and it still won't open. what does today's teaching suggest?
o: give up: it isn't for you.
keep living with it; understanding can take years.
games.why: even a people who saw wonders for forty years were only then given a heart to know.

practice: Think of one thing you don't understand yet: a text that won't open, a person whose choices puzzle you, a part of your own life that hasn't made sense.
Instead of pushing at it, set it down gently, like a seed in soil, and tell yourself it can take years. Notice whatever shifts, if anything does.
